items.title: The lost rucksack
items.dek: Anna loses her bag on a train — and worries most about her sandwich.
paragraphs: Mr Hall: Good morning, Leeds Station lost property. How can I help?
Anna: Hello. I think I've lost my rucksack. I was on the 9.15 train from York.
Mr Hall: I'm sorry to hear that. What does it look like?
Anna: It's dark green, with a small yellow bird on the front.
Mr Hall: Have you checked the train company's website?
Anna: Yes, I've already looked, but there's nothing there yet.
Mr Hall: What's inside the bag?
Anna: My laptop, a blue notebook and a cheese sandwich. I haven't eaten it yet!
Mr Hall: A cheese sandwich? Please wait a moment. I'll check the shelf.
Anna: Thank you. I've never lost anything on a train before. I feel terrible.
Mr Hall: Don't worry, it happens every day. Oh! I've just found a green rucksack with a yellow bird on it.
Anna: Really? That's mine! Has anyone opened it?
Mr Hall: Someone has handed it in, but nobody has opened it. And the sandwich is still inside.
Anna: Wonderful! Can I collect it today?
Mr Hall: Yes. We're open until five o'clock. Please bring some ID.
Anna: I will. I'm coming now! Please don't eat my sandwich.
Mr Hall: Don't worry. I've already had my lunch. It was a very small one, though.
paragraphs_zh: 霍尔先生：早上好，这里是利兹火车站失物招领处。有什么可以帮您？
安娜：你好。我想我把背包弄丢了。我坐的是从约克开来的9点15分那趟火车。
霍尔先生：真遗憾。它看起来什么样？
安娜：深绿色的，正面有一只黄色的小鸟。
霍尔先生：您查过火车公司的网站了吗？
安娜：查过了，我已经看过了，但那里还什么都没有。
安娜：我的笔记本电脑、一本蓝色笔记本和一个奶酪三明治。我还没吃呢！
霍尔先生：奶酪三明治？请稍等，我去看看架子上有没有。
安娜：谢谢。我以前从来没在火车上丢过东西。我觉得糟透了。
霍尔先生：别担心，这种事天天都有。哦！我刚刚找到了一个带黄色小鸟的绿色背包。
安娜：真的吗？那是我的！有人打开过吗？
霍尔先生：有人把它交了上来，但没有人打开过。三明治还在里面。
安娜：太好了！我今天能来取吗？
霍尔先生：可以。我们营业到五点。请带上身份证件。
安娜：好的。我马上过来！请别吃我的三明治。
霍尔先生：别担心，我已经吃过午饭了。不过那顿饭很小。

glossary.en: the place where lost things are kept until the owner comes
a bag that you carry on your back
you say this when someone tells you bad news
until now (used in negative sentences and questions)
a flat board on a wall where you put things
to give something to someone in charge
to go to a place and take something that is yours
a card or paper that shows who you are

items.grammar: We use the present perfect (have/has + past participle) to talk about the past when it matters now: “I've lost my rucksack” (I don't have it now). Use already for something done earlier (“I've already looked”), just for a very recent action (“I've just found it”), yet in negative sentences (“nothing there yet”) and never/ever for life experience (“I've never lost anything on a train before”).
items.grammar_zh: 现在完成时（have/has + 过去分词）用来谈论与现在有关的过去的事：“I've lost my rucksack”（现在包不在我身边）。already 表示已经做完（“I've already looked”），just 表示刚刚发生（“I've just found it”），yet 用在否定句里，意思是“还（没有）”，never/ever 用来说人生经历（“我以前从来没在火车上丢过东西”）。汉语常用“了”“过”表达，英语则要用 have/has + 过去分词。
questions: Why is Anna worried about her sandwich?
What does Mr Hall do when Anna describes her bag?
And you? Have you ever lost something important? What happened?
